title: Maximum Sum Circular Subarray
description: Brute force to optimized: modulo-indexed circular summation versus dual Kadane's passes combined via the total-minus-minimum reframing.

blocks.text: Given a CIRCULAR integer array nums (the end connects back to the start), return the maximum possible sum of a non-empty subarray, where the subarray may wrap around from the end of the array back to the beginning.

blocks.caption: The answer is either the best ordinary subarray, or the total minus the worst excluded middle stretch

blocks.text: Given a circular array nums, find the maximum sum of a non-empty subarray, where a subarray is allowed to wrap around from the end of the array back to the beginning.

blocks.title: Analogy: Picking the Best Arc Around a Circular Track of Numbered Signs
blocks.text: Like walking around a circular track lined with signs bearing positive and negative point values, and wanting to collect the highest possible total by walking along any single continuous arc (which might pass through the starting/finish line). Either the best arc never crosses the finish line at all (an ordinary stretch), or it does cross it, which is equivalent to taking every sign on the track EXCEPT for some single non-wrapping stretch in the middle; minimizing that excluded middle stretch maximizes the wrapping arc's total.

blocks.caption: Kadane's twice: once directly for the best stretch, once mirrored to find the worst stretch to exclude

blocks.text: When every element is negative, the "total minus minimum subarray" formula would incorrectly suggest excluding the entire array (leaving an empty, invalid subarray) as optimal. In this case, the correct answer is simply the best (least negative) ordinary subarray, found directly via standard Kadane's Algorithm without ever considering the wrap.
Before trying to simulate wraparound directly for every possible subarray, notice that any wrapping subarray has an exact non-wrapping complement.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: A subarray either wraps around the circular boundary or it doesn't. Non-wrapping subarrays are found exactly by standard Kadane's Algorithm, applied directly to nums.

Observation 2: A WRAPPING subarray, when viewed the other way, is exactly "the entire array, except for some contiguous, non-wrapping middle stretch that got excluded".

Observation 3: Since the total sum of nums is fixed, maximizing a wrapping subarray's sum is equivalent to MINIMIZING the excluded middle stretch's sum; this minimum is found by a second, mirrored Kadane's pass (tracking a running minimum instead of maximum).

Observation 4: The final answer is the larger of (the best non-wrapping subarray) and (total sum minus the minimum subarray sum) -- EXCEPT when every element is negative, in which case the minimum subarray sum equals the total itself, which would incorrectly suggest an empty (invalid) wrapping subarray; in that specific case, only the non-wrapping answer is valid.

Recognizing that a wrapping subarray is the complement of some ordinary "excluded middle" subarray reduces an apparently new circular problem to two familiar Kadane's passes plus one careful edge case.

This is dual Kadane's Algorithm (as in Maximum Absolute Sum of Any Subarray) combined with the total-minus-minimum reframing (as in Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards), plus one specific degenerate case requiring careful handling.
For every possible starting position and every possible length (up to the full array length), sum the corresponding circular stretch directly using modulo arithmetic.

items: For every possible starting index, and every possible length from 1 up to the full array length, sum the elements at that stretch, wrapping around via modulo indexing.
Track the maximum sum found across every starting index and length.

codes.python:
def max_subarray_sum_circular(nums):
    n = len(nums)
    best = nums[0]
    for start in range(n):
        total = 0
        for count in range(1, n + 1):                                     # try every possible length, wrapping around with modulo
            idx = (start + count - 1) % n
            total += nums[idx]
            best = max(best, total)
    return best


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(max_subarray_sum_circular([5, -3, 5]))

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: Modulo indexing ((start + count - 1) % n) directly implements the circular wraparound for any starting position and length.
Every length from 1 to n is tried explicitly, since the best wrapping subarray could be almost the entire circular array.
best only ever increases, tracking the highest sum found across every possible circular stretch.

blocks.text: Every possible circular stretch is checked directly via modulo-wrapped summation, so the correct maximum is always found.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n squared), since each of the n starting positions sums up to n possible lengths.
Space: O(1) extra.

Limitation: summing from scratch for every (start, length) pair ignores that both the best non-wrapping subarray and the best wrapping subarray (via its excluded-middle complement) can each be found independently in a single Kadane's-style linear pass.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text: The brute force checks every circular stretch directly with modulo indexing. Instead, run two Kadane's-style passes over the ordinary (non-circular) array simultaneously: one tracking the maximum subarray sum (curMax/maxSum, standard Kadane's), and one tracking the minimum subarray sum (curMin/minSum, mirrored Kadane's), while also accumulating the total sum. The final answer is the larger of maxSum and (total - minSum), except when maxSum itself is negative (meaning every element is negative), in which case only maxSum is valid, since wrapping would otherwise imply an empty subarray.

In a single pass, accumulate total, and simultaneously run standard Kadane's (curMax/maxSum) and mirrored Kadane's (curMin/minSum). After the pass, if maxSum is negative, return maxSum directly; otherwise return the maximum of maxSum and (total - minSum).
Run dual Kadane's passes (max and min) alongside a running total, then combine them with the wraparound-safety check.

blocks.title: Combining the results
blocks.text: maxSum = 7 (non-wrapping best, the whole array). total - minSum = 7 - (-3) = 10 (wrapping best, excluding just the middle -3). Since maxSum (7) is not negative, the answer is max(7, 10) = 10, matching the expected answer.

codes.python:
def max_subarray_sum_circular(nums):
    total = 0
    cur_max = 0
    max_sum = float('-inf')                                                # best NON-wrapping subarray sum (standard Kadane's)
    cur_min = 0
    min_sum = float('inf')                                                 # worst (most negative) subarray sum, used to find the best WRAPPING subarray
    for x in nums:
        total += x
        cur_max = max(cur_max + x, x)
        max_sum = max(max_sum, cur_max)
        cur_min = min(cur_min + x, x)
        min_sum = min(min_sum, cur_min)
    if max_sum < 0:
        return max_sum                                                     # all elements negative: excluding everything isn't allowed, so don't wrap
    return max(max_sum, total - min_sum)                                   # best of: no wrap, or wrap (total minus the worst excluded middle)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(max_subarray_sum_circular([5, -3, 5]))

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n), a single pass tracking total, maxSum, and minSum together, with O(1) work per element.
Space: O(1) extra.

Every subarray is either entirely non-wrapping (found by standard Kadane's, giving maxSum) or wraps around, in which case it consists of exactly the elements NOT in some single non-wrapping "excluded middle" stretch; since the total is fixed, maximizing the wrapping subarray is the same as minimizing that excluded stretch, found by mirrored Kadane's (giving minSum). The one exception is when every element is negative: here, minSum equals the total itself (the "best" minimum is to exclude everything), which would make total - minSum equal 0, incorrectly suggesting an empty subarray is achievable; since an empty subarray isn't allowed, this case must fall back to maxSum directly.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Case","What happens"],"rows":[["maxSum < 0 (every element is negative)","Return maxSum directly; wrapping would otherwise incorrectly suggest excluding the entire array"],["maxSum >= 0","Return the larger of maxSum (best non-wrapping) and total - minSum (best wrapping)"]]}

items: curMax/maxSum and curMin/minSum are updated in the exact same single pass, using mirrored recurrences (max(x, cur+x) versus min(x, cur+x)).
total is accumulated independently, simply summing every element as they're visited.
The maxSum < 0 check must happen AFTER the full pass completes, since it depends on the final value of maxSum across the whole array.

blocks.text: This problem combines two previously-seen techniques: dual Kadane's passes (max and min, as in Maximum Absolute Sum of Any Subarray) and the total-minus-extremum reframing (as in Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards), plus one crucial degenerate case requiring careful handling.

items: Forgetting the all-negative edge case entirely, which causes an incorrect answer of 0 (an invalid empty subarray) instead of the correct, least-negative single element.
Using modulo-indexed circular simulation instead of recognizing the wrap = total-minus-excluded-middle reframing, leading to an unnecessarily complex or slow solution.
Computing minSum with the wrong sign convention (e.g., trying to track -curMax instead of a properly mirrored curMin recurrence), leading to subtly incorrect results.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Edge case","Expected behavior"],"rows":[["Every element in nums is negative","The answer is the single largest (least negative) element, found via maxSum alone"],["nums has only 1 element","The answer is that element itself, whether positive or negative"],["nums is entirely positive","The answer equals the sum of the entire array (both the non-wrapping and wrapping computations agree here)"]]}

items: State the "wrapping subarray is the complement of some non-wrapping excluded stretch" reframing explicitly and early, since it's the single insight that unlocks the entire two-Kadane's-passes solution; then flag the all-negative edge case as a natural follow-up, showing you've fully reasoned through the approach's boundaries.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: "Maximum subarray sum, but the array is CIRCULAR" points toward running Kadane's Algorithm twice (once for max, once mirrored for min), combined via total - minSum for the wrapping case, with careful handling for the all-negative edge case.

items: How would you also report the actual subarray (and whether it wraps)? Track tentative boundaries for both the max and min Kadane's passes, and reconstruct indices based on which of maxSum or total - minSum wins.

What if the subarray were also required to have a bounded length? This would need a different technique entirely, likely a deque-based sliding window maximum over a bounded-length prefix-sum difference, since Kadane's recurrence alone doesn't track length.

How does this generalize to "maximum circular subarray PRODUCT" instead of sum? Product introduces sign-flipping complications (a very negative product times another negative becomes very positive), requiring a substantially different dual max/min tracking approach even for the non-circular version.

Combines dual Kadane's Algorithm (as in Maximum Absolute Sum of Any Subarray) with the total-minus-extremum reframing (as in Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards), specifically adapted for circular wraparound.

blocks.text:
Brute force: O(n squared) time, O(1) space.
Optimized (dual Kadane's + total, with edge-case handling): O(n) time, O(1) space.

items: Pattern: Dual Kadane's Algorithm (max and min) combined with a running total, plus a special all-negative edge case
Core Idea: A wrapping subarray is the complement of some non-wrapping excluded stretch; maximizing it means minimizing that excluded stretch
Time: O(n)
Space: O(1)
